			{ path: 'module', loadChildren: () => SubModule },
		])

SubModule:

		])

...

		TestService
	],
```

Each time I navigate between /module/test1 and /module/test2 - TestService constructor is called

**Expected behavior**
If test1 and test2 are defined as routes in RootModule, only one instance of TestService is created. I expect SubModule to inject the same instance of TestService if I navigate between its components.

If I move TestService provider to RootModule - works as expected

Most of components of one of modules uses a service that opens and maintains WebSocket connection. Each time a service is spawned, new connection is opened. I definitely want to reuse the component and keep single connection open than close and reopen it every time user navigates between pages.

issue.title: Provider.useFactory called multiple times
issue.body:

[ ] feature request
[ ] support request => Please do not submit support request here, instead see https://github.com/angular/angular/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md#question
```

**Current behavior**
When upgrading from Angular 2.1.2 to the current 2.2.3, the semantics of an NgModule provider changed, when it was using the useFactory property. In 2.1.2, the factory method was only called once and effectively gave a singleton to each injection point within the NgModule. Now, it is being called multiple times for each injection point.
Is this expected?

**Expected behavior**
The Provider.useFactory is only called one time per NgModule and all injection points in components it is injected into.

**Please tell us about your environment:**
OS: Windows 7 x64
IDE: IntelliJ IDEA Ultimate 2016.3
Package Manager: npm 4.0.2
TypeScript: 2.0.10

* **Angular version:** 2.2.3

* **Browser:** Chrome 54.0.2840.99 m (64-bit)
 
* **Language:** TypeScript 2.0.10 ES2015

body: Having the exact same problem as described by [@serhiisol](https://github.com/angular/angular/issues/12869#issuecomment-261217933) after upgrading from Angular 2.1.2 and Router 3.1.2 to Angular 2.2.3 and Router 3.2.3.

Hi Guys,

We need to start using some new features on FormGroup (2.2.0) but are blocked by this issue.

Can someone from the Angular team advise when this will be resolved. The issue appears to exist in 2.2.3 and the latest 2.3.0 beta.

- Are there any known workarounds?
- Is it something we need to change in our code?

Regards,
Tarek

Attached is a angular-cli project which exactly reproduces the bug as I see it.
It has a lazy route which, when loaded, leads to the module being loaded _twice_, as is shown by the console.log() in the `src/app/lazy.module.ts` file:
[router-bug.zip](https://github.com/angular/angular/files/619860/router-bug.zip)

In order to run, use:
- npm install angular-cli -g
- npm install
- ng serve
- goto localhost:4200/
- click on the "Call me Lazy" link

We _strongly_ depend on the Angular team fixing this bug, and I am quite amazed that all we get in response is: "Pls add a repro in plunkr."
This kind of bug should be put to high priority I think, need patch update soon

I thought I was the only one with this issue but clearly I'm not, let's hope they fix it soon :/

Btw I also have another [plnkr](http://embed.plnkr.co/lLy27VGKucLDqsOa7FQj/), just in case (modified tour of heroes, just click the Heroes button and you can see the 2 calls in the console)

This is why it is happening.

* Say we have two modules Parent and Child, where Child is loaded lazily. 
* Say we have two components ParentCmp1 and ParentCmp2 defined in Parent, and ChildCmp1 defined in Child.
* Say typically the components form the following tree when instantiated: ParentCmp1 => ParentCmp2 => ChildCmp1.
* Finally, say ChildCmp1 injects ParentCmp2.

Since we run guards and resolvers before instantiating components (this is one of the guarantees the router provides to make component instantiation atomic), we can only constructor the following injector tree:

```
Injector for Parent => Injector for Child.
```

When instantiating components, the injector tree has to look like this:

```
Injector for Parent => Injector for ParentCmp1 => Injector for ParentCmp2 => Injector for Child => Injector for ChildCmp1
```

Because we have two injector trees, we instantiate the module twice. One module cannot be a node in two trees, it cannot be used in two contexts.

@vicb what do you think is a good solution? we can add a new property something like loadGuards in addition to loadChildren, so it's possible to provision two modules (one for preActivation, and the other one for activation).

Hi Victor,

Thanks for the info.

Do you know what was changed in 2.2.0 to break the previous experience? In 2.1.0 this was not a issue?

Also, what is really the primary reason behind creating different DI contexts for lazy loaded modules. As they seem to be creating more friction than benefits. 

I would imagine that in a large majority of applications, the authors of the lazy loaded modules are part of the same project. So the modules that are being lazy loaded are known to them.

The issue of overwriting providers can be managed by communication within the team and some sort of angular warning. Many of us came from Angular 1 where we only had a single DI context and we were mostly ok.

IMHO, I would much prefer having a setting that enables the use of a single DI context for all modules including lazy loaded modules. 

This would eliminate the need for -
- ForRoot
- ForChild
- loadGuards option (indicates detailed knowledge of the lazy loaded module anyway)

Regards,
Tarek
